label: DS1-agent-security-taxonomy
prompt: CONTEXT: preparing a security-hardening audit of a personal AI AGENT (voice+text, full bash + document-parsing + screen-reading + multi-lane sub-agents, a regex confirm-gate). You are ONE research lane feeding a Fable-5 mastermind. TASK: give a dense, current threat taxonomy for LLM-agent security that we can check our system against. Cover: prompt-injection via TOOL OUTPUTS / parsed documents / fetched web content (indirect injection), the confused-deputy problem, HITL confirm-gate weaknesses (why matching the agent's own command string is insufficient), taint-tracking / provenance of untrusted content, capability-based security vs pattern/regex gates, sandboxing + reduced-capability modes for unattended agents, exfiltration of secrets/credentials, and supply-chain risk in auto-run hooks. For EACH threat: the mechanism + the standard mitigation. END with two lists: MUST-HAVE mitigations for an agent with our capabilities, and OVER-ENGINEERING to avoid. Mark claims HARD-FACT vs RECALLED-PATTERN.

label: DS2-debloat-methods
prompt: CONTEXT: a large personal AI-OS codebase (~600 scripts, 44 hooks, 100+ skills, 300+ memory files) has grown bloated; we want to de-bloat it SAFELY without breaking live paths, feeding a Fable-5 mastermind cut. You are ONE research lane. TASK: survey proven methods for large-codebase de-bloat: dead-code / orphan detection (static import graphs, call-graph reachability, dynamic-usage logs), safe-deletion workflows (deprecation markers, staged removal, revertability), architectural-coherence audits (identifying overlapping/duplicate subsystems and choosing a canonical one), and how to distinguish 'unused' from 'load-bearing-but-rarely-called'. Emphasize how to AVOID deleting something live (the expensive mistake). END with a concrete SAFE-CUT CHECKLIST + BUILD/CUT lists. Mark HARD-FACT vs RECALLED-PATTERN.

label: DS3-minimal-safe-autonomy
prompt: CONTEXT: a personal AI agent is becoming more autonomous (overnight unattended runs, parallel sub-agent dispatch, acting on the owner's machine). We want it SIMPLER but MORE POWERFUL and SAFE, feeding a Fable-5 mastermind. You are ONE research lane. TASK: survey patterns for minimal-but-safe agent autonomy: reduced-capability / least-privilege profiles for unattended vs attended mode, reversible-by-default action design, trust boundaries between the orchestrator and sub-agents, when a human-in-the-loop confirm is truly required vs friction, budget/rate governance for unattended runs, and how autonomy compounds risk if trust outpaces verification. END with: the minimal safe-autonomy design for an agent like this, and the autonomy features that are premature/over-engineering. Mark HARD-FACT vs RECALLED-PATTERN.
